extracted.intended_audience: journalists, public relations professionals, university communications officers, PRSSA/PRSA members and students
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplar structure for an organizational press release announcing a new chapter/partnership, showing required elements (headline, dateline, lead, quotes, boilerplate, contacts). Useful for PR practitioners preparing similar announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline
rubrics_metrics.description: "PRSSA Expands Global Reach in the United States and Mexico"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise, descriptive headline that states the main news. Use present-tense verb phrasing and proper capitalization. Should be attention-grabbing while clearly conveying the announcement (e.g., expansion, partnership, launch). Avoid vague or overly long headlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subheadline / Standfirst
rubrics_metrics.description: "William Paterson University and Universidad de las Américas Puebla Join Growing Roster of PRSSA Chapters"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short supporting line under the headline that names key parties or summarizes the specific development. Provides more detail than the headline and orients the reader to the parties involved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline (city, date)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the city and date at the start of the body to indicate where and when the release originates. Use full month name and year. Dateline signals official timing and location for reporters and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph summarizing the news (who/what/where/when/why)
rubrics_metrics.description: First paragraph: "PRSSA, the foremost organization for students interested in the public relations and communications fields, announced today it has added Universidad de las Américas Puebla (UDLAP) ... and William Paterson University (WP) to its network of Chapters worldwide. ... This is the first PRSSA Chapter established in Mexico."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Open with the most important facts: the organization, the action taken, the institutions involved, and any notable 'firsts' or scope. The lead should give readers enough to understand the story without reading further.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quotes from leaders with clear attribution and credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: quotes by Joseph Abreu, APR, CPRC, 2024 PRSA Chair; statements by Dr. Judith Cruz-Sandoval and Professor Lorra Brown, MA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include at least one quote from an organizational leader or local stakeholder that explains significance, reaction, or expected impact. Always include full name, title, and credentials/affiliations for credibility. Quotes should add perspective beyond the factual lead (e.g., value to students, institutional benefits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting context and organizational background
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements such as "PRSSA has a presence at universities and colleges across the United States and in Argentina, Colombia, Peru and Puerto Rico" and historical context about PRSSA and the Bateman Case Study Competition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context that situates the announcement within the organization's history, reach, or mission. Include relevant background (scope of operations, longevity, signature programs) so readers understand significance and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local support and named advisers / partners
rubrics_metrics.description: "Support for the Chapter at UDLAP will be provided by PRSA San Diego/Imperial Counties. PRSA member Dr. Judith Cruz-Sandoval will serve as faculty adviser and Dr. Mauricio Graciano will serve as professional adviser."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify local chapters, partner organizations, and named individuals who will support or advise the initiative. This demonstrates operational backing and gives reporters/local stakeholders contacts and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate 'About' sections for organizations mentioned
rubrics_metrics.description: Sections titled "About PRSSA", "About Universidad de las Américas Puebla", and "About William Paterson University" containing concise institutional descriptions and website links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief, standardized description (boilerplate) for each organization referenced, with mission, scale, notable programs, and a URL for more information. Boilerplates help editors quickly add background copy to stories and ensure factual consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information for media inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact block listing names and titles: "Linda Beltran, Chief Communications Officer; Courtney Vance, Communications Manager; Public Relations Society of America Inc., 120 Wall Street, 21st Fl., New York, NY 10005-4024."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide at least one media contact with name, title, organization, and mailing address (and preferably phone/email). Make it easy for journalists to follow up. If available, include multiple contacts (press officer, local contact).

rubrics_metrics.name: End/closing marker
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a clear end marker (e.g., ### or -30-) to indicate the release is complete. This prevents accidental copying of navigation or other web content when republishing and signals to editors that no additional text follows.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of specific facts, numbers, and program details to substantiate claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples: "With over 13 courses allied to the public relations sequence...", "WP marks the 11th PRSSA Chapter established in New Jersey", "40 nationalities represented on campus".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support claims with concrete data (counts, rankings, program offerings, geographic reach) to lend credibility. Quantifiable detail helps reporters and readers understand scale and impact; avoid unsupported hyperbole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and logistical detail for institutional context
rubrics_metrics.description: Descriptions such as UDLAP location in Cholula, proximity to Mexico City and Puebla, and WP campus acreage and distance from NYC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When announcing institutions, include geographic and logistical details (city, campus size, proximity to major cities, cultural or historic notes) that are useful for local media and provide color for storytelling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear naming of academic programs and student opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Mentions of degrees and courses: "students can pursue degrees in communication and media production and communication and public relations", "BA in public relations and MA in integrated marketing communication programs".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List relevant academic programs, degrees, or student opportunities tied to the announcement. This informs prospective students and helps education reporters link the news to curriculum and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional tone and factual, third-person voice
rubrics_metrics.description: Release text uses formal third-person description and factual statements, punctuated by attributed quotes for opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a professional, objective tone. Use third-person narrative for organizational facts and reserve first-person-like language for attributed quotes. Avoid overly promotional language unsupported by facts.
